ingredients.item: boneless, skin-on chicken thighs, butterflied to an even 1.5 cm
ingredients.preparation: skin on renders and crisps; skinless works, glaze harder

ingredients.item: Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, cold oi muchim , kimchi , pickled radish cubes

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Skin side down first on a medium fire — the skin renders slowly into its own fat bath and crisps while the paste on the meat side stays safe above it. Six to eight minutes, undisturbed, while the fat builds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the skin releases on its own when it is deep golden and crisp; if it is still welded, it is not done. Never force the flip early.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: Flip to the paste side, 4–5 minutes. The glaze sets in the rendered fat's heat; watch the edges, where it blackens first. Any flare-up: move the piece to the cool corner for 30 seconds, back to finish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: pull when the center of a test piece is opaque and its juices run clear — no pink, chicken's absolute rule — and the glaze is brick-glossy, charred only at the very fat edge.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Rest 3 minutes, scissors into strips across the thigh, sesame over, platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: eating test: crisp skin snap, then the juicy paste-glazed meat, heat blooming after the sweet — and the cold cucumber between bites resetting the palate. That triangle is the record.

storageNotes: Marinated thighs keep 24 hours. Cooked, 3 days — cold strips over hot rice, or chopped into a spicy chicken fried rice with the leftover glaze.

Variations: the soy-pear fork (#M16); the same marinade on wings, double-glazed in the last minutes, is the tabletop's snack lane; thinned and brushed on the shrimp record (#SF01) for the spicy table.
